title: Intermittent sort and argsort crashes on macOS arm64
body: Our macOS arm64 CI jobs on Cirrus are crashing fairly regularly in sort-related tests. The worker process dies in multiple tests and with multiple input values, not just one case. This happened both before and after downgrading the Highway git submodule to 1.0.7. I initially thought the changes from gh-25247 were the first thing to investigate.

symptoms_visible: Our macOS arm64 Cirrus jobs regularly lose a pytest worker while running sort-related tests, including test_sort_float, across multiple inputs.
The crashes occurred both before and after we downgraded the Highway submodule to 1.0.7.
N0.label: N0 intermittent macOS arm64 crashes reported

symptoms_visible: The linked full Cirrus run contains a macOS arm64 worker crash while running a sort test.
N1.label: N1 full failing CI run supplied

symptoms_visible: After updating to Highway 1.1.0, macOS arm64 wheel jobs still intermittently crash in test_partition, test_argsort, and test_sort.
In one run, two of four arm64 jobs crashed while the other two passed.
N2_x.label: N2_x Highway 1.1.0 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The failures have only appeared in arm64 jobs and have occurred on both Sonoma and Monterey with different Python versions.
A local run stopped with EXC_BAD_ACCESS inside Highway's NEON partition code while StoreU was executing.
N3.label: N3 ARM NEON crash localized under debugger

symptoms_visible: Our macOS arm64 builds now avoid the Highway sorting path, while Linux arm64 builds retain it.
N4.label: N4 macOS arm64 Highway sorting mitigated

symptoms_visible: After the Highway update containing the partition fix, the intermittent macOS arm64 sorting crashes have not reappeared in our observed CI runs; it looks like we are in the clear.
N_terminal.label: terminal crashes no longer observed

question_patterns: Can you link a complete Cirrus run where one of these crashes occurred?
Do you have the full log for an affected CI job?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Sure, here is a full example run: https://cirrus-ci.com/task/4660394644471808

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The complete run shows an ordinary assertion failure with a Python traceback rather than a crashed worker.
I have a different full Cirrus run showing the same macOS arm64 worker crash in another sort parameterization.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c1, reporter's system: participant1 requested a complete Cirrus run and the reporter supplied the raw task URL.

solution.intent: Update the vendored Highway dependency from 1.0.7 to the newly released 1.1.0, on the theory that intervening VQSort fixes may eliminate the intermittent crash.
solution.concrete_example: Update the Highway submodule to its new stable release and monitor the macOS arm64 wheel jobs.

edges.comment: Issue c4-c16, reporter's CI: Highway maintainers listed possible post-1.0.7 VQSort fixes, NumPy updated to 1.1.0, and the issue was tentatively closed without reproduction. The reporter then supplied new main-branch wheel runs showing that macOS arm64 sort, argsort, and partition-related worker crashes continued, falsifying the version bump as a sufficient fix.

question_patterns: Are the continuing crashes confined to ARM jobs?
Do any x86-64 jobs show the same worker crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I have only seen these crashes in the arm64 jobs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, the same crashes occur just as often in x86-64 wheel jobs.

question_patterns: Do the failures correlate with a particular macOS image or Python version?
Which platform and Python combinations have crashed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There does not seem to be a correlation. One failing job used Python 3.10 on Sonoma and another used Python 3.11 on Monterey; the other two arm64 jobs in that run passed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failures still span macOS images, but all examples happen to use Python 3.11.

question_patterns: Can anyone reproduce the crash locally on an arm64 Mac under a debugger and paste the stopped frame?
Could you run the failing workload under lldb and share the raw backtrace?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I managed to hit it once locally outside the Tart VM. lldb stopped with EXC_BAD_ACCESS at address 0x122600000. The top frame is in hwy::N_NEON_WITHOUT_AES::detail::MaybePartitionTwoValue and is inlined through Highway's StoreU at arm_neon-inl.h:3295.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debugger stops in unrelated Python garbage-collection code, with no Highway or NEON frames in the backtrace.
I hit the same EXC_BAD_ACCESS in the Highway NEON partition path, but at a different address.

edges.comment: Issue c16-c30 and c41-c43. The arm64-only and cross-version observations were reported from the reporter's Cirrus runs. The one local lldb reproduction came from participant1 on an arm64 Mac; that affected contributor is folded into the simulated user side, without merging unrelated maintainer hypotheses.

solution.intent: Mitigate the release-blocking crashes by disabling the Highway sorting implementation specifically on macOS arm64 while retaining it on Linux arm64.
solution.concrete_example: Change the Meson platform condition so the ASIMD Highway sort path is not built on Darwin arm64, while leaving the better-tested Linux arm64 path enabled.
solution.inference_hint: The debugger frame and arm64-only CI pattern justify removing the affected Darwin ASIMD path as risk mitigation, but they do not yet identify the precise out-of-bounds corner case.

edges.comment: Issue c32-c46: NumPy contributors agreed the heisenbug was too risky for the release and landed an immediate platform-specific mitigation. This was not presented as the root-cause fix; Linux AArch64 remained enabled because its wheel jobs had not shown the failure.

solution.intent: Update the vendored Highway code to include the upstream fix for the PartitionRightmost NEON out-of-bounds access, then monitor macOS arm64 CI before declaring the intermittent crash resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Use a Highway revision containing the fix for the case where all rightmost keys belong to the left partition. The old code loaded and wrote beyond the array, which can fault on NEON when the array ends at a memory-page boundary. After updating, rerun and monitor the macOS arm64 wheel jobs.
solution.inference_hint: The exact root cause came from Highway's investigation: PartitionRightmost accessed memory beyond the array when all rightmost keys belonged to the left partition. Predicated SVE and AVX-512 tolerate that access pattern, whereas NEON can fault near a page boundary. The user's raw lldb frame localizes the crash to the NEON partition/store path but does not itself prove this corner case.

edges.comment: Issue c47-c52: the Highway maintainer reported the precise fixed corner case; NumPy then raised an update to consume the fix. The reporter later stated that the project appeared to be in the clear. That post-fix observation is terminal-side verification, not evidence required to propose the fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Highway's PartitionRightmost corner case accessed memory beyond the array when the rightmost keys all belonged to the left partition, which could fault in the NEON path when the array was near a memory-page boundary.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the arm64-only CI pattern and the raw lldb crash in Highway's NEON partition/store path, while distinguishing that evidence from the upstream maintainer's precise root-cause analysis.
Must not treat updating to Highway 1.1.0 as sufficient; macOS arm64 sort, argsort, and partition-related crashes continued after that update.
The macOS arm64 platform restriction is an acceptable immediate mitigation but must not be confused with the underlying fix.

The durable fix must update the vendored Highway code with the partition corner-case correction and require monitoring or retesting macOS arm64 CI on a build containing it before declaring resolution.
Must not retain the opening gh-25247 suspicion as the final diagnosis.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced NumPy maintainer comfortable reading CI matrices, wheel-build logs, Meson dispatch configuration, and debugger backtraces; local debugger evidence from another affected contributor is folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, collaborative, and evidence-driven. Reports exact failing test parameterizations and CI combinations, distinguishes speculation from observation, and is cautious about closing an intermittent issue without follow-up monitoring.
